prerequisites: Good computer skills at user level
Strong oral and written communication skills
Minimum knowledge of English for understanding some readings and potential use of software practices

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and ability to organize and direct companies.
Knowledge and abilities in strategy and planning applied to different organizational structures.
Knowledge of commercial and labor law.
Knowledge of financial and cost accounting.
Knowledge of management information systems, industrial organization, production and logistics systems, and quality management systems.
Abilities for work organization and human resource management. Knowledge of occupational risk prevention.
Ability to design, construct, and operate industrial plants.
Ability to design and organize the documentation of a Management System, as well as to monitor it.
Ability to apply basic management skills in strategy, planning, decision-making, and control of action plans.
Understand and develop labor hiring and training management needs in the company.
Understand basic management control techniques through analysis of balance sheets, costs, and financial indicators.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to Business Management and Strategic Planning.
Financial Analysis. Balance Sheets. Budgets. Project Valuation and financial strategy in the European Union.
Data-driven Business Management in practice: Systems for Control and Decision Making.

PRACTICAL CONTENTS: Design, analysis, and discussion in different exercises and assignments on various types of indicators (KPIs) for business management control based on databases or quantitative information on HR, Internal Processes, Customer Satisfaction (based on survey design), business valuation. PowerBI

assessment_methods.method: Final exam of the subject (Theoretical Block)
Laboratory practices corresponding to the first module (Practical Block)
Submission and presentation of a work related to the second module (Practical Block)
Practical in-class exercise of the third module based on a real business case and use of software tools (Practical Block)

assessment_rules: The ordinary evaluation is divided into two blocks: Theoretical (Exam) and Practical (Practical Activities). A minimum grade of 4/10 is required for each block. If the minimums are met, the final grade is calculated as (0.6 × Exam) + (0.4 × Practical Activities). Otherwise, the final grade will be the minimum between the calculated grade and 4.0. In extraordinary calls, the same evaluation system applies; if the Practical Block minimum was met in the ordinary call, that grade is retained for two subsequent extraordinary calls.
